html:
Tipu Sultan was the ruler of Mysore in south India from 1782 to 1799, and the most stubborn enemy of the British East India Company in the south.

He was the son of Hyder Ali, a soldier who had taken power in Mysore. Father and son fought four Anglo Mysore Wars against the Company and its allies:

  • In the first two they held their own, and in 1780 they destroyed a British army at Pollilur.
  • In the third, 1790 to 1792, Tipu lost half his kingdom.
  • In the fourth, in 1799, the British stormed his capital Srirangapatna, and Tipu died fighting at the walls.

He modernised hard. He sought help from France and wrote to Napoleon, drilled his army in European style, used the iron Mysorean rockets, issued new coins and pushed silk farming.

His memory is divided. Many in India see a freedom fighter. Others recall his forced conversions and deportations of Hindus and Christians in Malabar, Coorg and Mangalore. His wooden mechanical tiger mauling a European soldier, Tipu's Tiger, is in a London museum.
sum: Tipu Sultan was the ruler of Mysore in south India from 1782 to 1799, and the most stubborn enemy of the British East India Company in the south.
